extracted.intended_audience: graduate students and researchers learning algebraic geometry (readers of Vakil's text)
extracted.subtask_description: Definitions, properties, and standard results about I‑filtrations, the Artin–Rees Lemma, and quasicoherent/locally free/coherent sheaves (vector bundles) on schemes; includes exercises giving constructions and structural criteria. Aimed at understanding when sheaves are locally free, how they behave in exact sequences, and standard tensor/dual/determinant constructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: I-filtration
rubrics_metrics.description: A descending filtration M = M0 ⊃ M1 ⊃ M2 ⊃ ··· is called an I-filtration (for an ideal I of A).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: the I-adic filtration Mk = I^k M. (Text gives the formal condition and uses this notion in the Artin–Rees discussion.)

rubrics_metrics.name: I-stable filtration
rubrics_metrics.description: An I-filtration is I-stable if for some s and all d, n ≥ 0, I^d M_s = M_{s+d}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: the I-adic filtration is I-stable. This stability notion is central to the equivalence with finite generation of the Rees module.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rees algebra/module finite generation ↔ I-stability (Proposition 13.9.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: For A Noetherian and M a finitely generated A-module, the graded module M• (⊕_{n≥0} M_n) is a finitely generated module over A• (⊕_{n≥0} I^n) if and only if the filtration is I-stable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses Noetherianness of A• and the equivalence shows finite generation of the Rees module is the algebraic criterion for I-stability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Artin–Rees Lemma (13.9.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Suppose A is Noetherian and (M_n) is an I-stable filtration of a finitely generated A-module M. If L ⊂ M is a submodule and L_n := L ∩ M_n, then (L_n) is an I-stable filtration of L.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This lemma generalizes the intuition that analytically zero functions vanish in a neighborhood; it is used later (e.g., Cohomology and Base Change).

rubrics_metrics.name: Corollary on intersections (13.9.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Suppose I is an ideal of a Noetherian ring A and M is a finitely generated A-module, and L ⊂ M is a submodule. Then for some integer s, I^d(L ∩ I^s M) = L ∩ I^{d+s} M for all d ≥ 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Warning: it need not be true that I^d L = L ∩ I^d M for all d; the corollary gives the corrected stable equality after shifting by s.

rubrics_metrics.name: Krull intersection style assertion (Exercise 13.9.A)
rubrics_metrics.description: If I is an ideal of a Noetherian ring A and M is finitely generated, statements about ∩_{j=1}^∞ I^j M = 0 under suitable hypotheses (and related Nakayama hints).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise applies Artin–Rees and Nakayama to establish vanishing of intersections in standard cases (e.g., local rings or domains).

rubrics_metrics.name: Free sheaf and rank
rubrics_metrics.description: A free sheaf on a ringed space X is an O_X-module isomorphic to ⊕_{I} O_X; its rank is the cardinality of the index set (agrees with rank at a point).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the sheaf analogue of free modules; rank may vary on connected components or be infinite.

rubrics_metrics.name: Locally free sheaf = vector bundle (definition / equivalence)
rubrics_metrics.description: A locally free sheaf is an O_X-module that is locally isomorphic to a free sheaf; this notion corresponds (equivalently) to vector bundles via local trivializations and transition functions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text explains the equivalence by giving transition functions and sheaf-of-sections viewpoint; see Exercises relating the perspectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vector bundle trivialization condition
rubrics_metrics.description: A rank n vector bundle π: V → M has for each p an open U and a homeomorphism φ: U × R^n → π^{-1}(U) (compatible with projection) giving local triviality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The trivialization identifies sections over U with n-tuples of functions; if U = M the bundle is trivial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transition functions and cocycle condition
rubrics_metrics.description: Given trivializations on a cover {U_i}, the transition functions T_{ij} ∈ GL_n(O(U_i ∩ U_j)) must satisfy the cocycle condition T_{ij}|_{U_i∩U_k} = T_{ik}|_{U_i∩U_k} · T_{kj}|_{U_i∩U_k}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conversely, data of a cover and transition functions satisfying the cocycle condition determine the vector bundle (up to unique isomorphism).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sheaf of sections is an O_X-module
rubrics_metrics.description: The sheaf of sections F of a vector bundle is an O_X-module; given a trivialization over U, sections over U identify with n-tuples of functions on U.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This identification is used throughout to relate geometric and sheaf-theoretic perspectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transition functions for sheaf of sections (compatibility)
rubrics_metrics.description: If ⃗s_i and ⃗s_j are representations of the same section over U_i and U_j, then on overlaps Tij ⃗s_i = ⃗s_j.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 14.2.A asks to verify this carefully (watch indices).

rubrics_metrics.name: Invertible sheaf = line bundle
rubrics_metrics.description: A rank 1 locally free sheaf is called an invertible sheaf (or line bundle); invertibility can be characterized by the existence of G with F ⊗_OX G ≅ O_X.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Author notes 'invertible sheaf' is an awkward term; many use 'line bundle' informally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pullback preserves locally free sheaves and rank (Exercise 14.2.B/C)
rubrics_metrics.description: If π: X → Y is a morphism of ringed spaces then π^*(⊕^n O_Y) ≅ ⊕^n O_X; if G is locally free of rank n on Y then π^* G is locally free of rank n on X, and transition matrices pull back: transition matrices become π^* T_{ij}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercises guide constructing trivializations for π^*G and verifying transition matrices are pulled back.

rubrics_metrics.name: Locally free sheaves are not an abelian category
rubrics_metrics.description: Locally free sheaves (vector bundles) with natural O_X-linear maps do not form an abelian category because cokernels of maps between locally free sheaves need not be locally free.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: multiplication by t on the trivial line bundle over R jumps rank; cokernel fails to be a vector bundle. This motivates quasicoherent sheaves.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quasicoherent sheaves form the smallest local abelian subcategory containing vector bundles
rubrics_metrics.description: Quasicoherent sheaves are defined as the smallest abelian subcategory of Mod_OX that is 'local' and includes vector bundles (equivalently, OX-modules locally cokernels of maps between free sheaves).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This enlarges the category so kernels/cokernels behave well; coherent sheaves refine this in locally Noetherian settings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relation among categories (inclusion diagram)
rubrics_metrics.description: Mod_OX (abelian) ⊃ quasicoherent sheaves (abelian) ⊃ locally free sheaves (not abelian); and in the Noetherian setting quasicoherent ⊃ coherent ⊃ finite rank locally free.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Helps position locally free sheaves relative to better-behaved categories for homological algebra.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hom of locally free sheaves is locally free (Exercise 14.2.C)
rubrics_metrics.description: If F and G are locally free sheaves of ranks m and n respectively, then Hom_OX(F, G) is a locally free sheaf of rank mn.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a basic construction used to form duals and endomorphism sheaves.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dual of a locally free sheaf (Exercise 14.2.D)
rubrics_metrics.description: If E is locally free of (finite) rank n then E^∨ := Hom(E, O_X) is locally free of rank n; for rank 1, transition functions invert; also E ≅ E^{∨∨} canonically (but canonical iso need not equal arbitrary isomorphisms).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Caveat: some locally free sheaves are not isomorphic to their duals (example: O(1) on P^n).

rubrics_metrics.name: Tensor product of locally free sheaves is locally free (Exercise 14.2.E)
rubrics_metrics.description: If F and G are locally free sheaves, then F ⊗ G is locally free; if F is invertible, F^∨ ≅ O_X implies invertibility properties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tensor product is the standard way to combine bundles; see Exercise 14.2.F for exactness properties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tensoring by a locally free sheaf is exact (Exercise 14.2.F)
rubrics_metrics.description: If 0 → G' → G → G'' → 0 is exact and F is locally free, then 0 → G' ⊗ F → G ⊗ F → G'' ⊗ F → 0 is exact (tensoring by a locally free sheaf is an exact functor).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hint: check exactness on stalks where locally free sheaf is free, using identification of stalks of tensor product.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hom-tensor adjunction involving duals (Exercise 14.2.G)
rubrics_metrics.description: If E is locally free of finite rank and F,G are OX-modules, then Hom(F ⊗ E, G) ≅ Hom(F, G ⊗ E^∨) ≅ Hom(F, Hom(E, G)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proved first in the free case and then localized; standard adjunction used widely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Picard group definition and functoriality (Exercise 14.2.H/I/J)
rubrics_metrics.description: Invertible sheaves up to isomorphism form an abelian group under tensor product, denoted Pic X. Pullback gives Pic a contravariant functor from ringed spaces to Ab; analytiﬁcation induces Pic homomorphisms for complex varieties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercises show group structure, functoriality, and compatibility with analytification in the complex algebraic case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Locally free sheaves on schemes need not be locally trivial on small opens
rubrics_metrics.description: Contrary to expectation from manifolds, on schemes (Zariski topology) invertible or locally free sheaves may be nontrivial on every nonempty open (example: certain elliptic curve open subsets).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This highlights the coarse nature of the Zariski topology and motivates use of cohomological invariants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Locally free sheaves are quasicoherent; finite rank locally free are finite type and (when OX is coherent) coherent
rubrics_metrics.description: Every locally free sheaf on a scheme is quasicoherent; finite rank locally free sheaves are finite type, and if OX is coherent then they are coherent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful to know which finiteness/regularity properties are automatic for vector bundles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subsheaf of a locally free sheaf need not be a subvector bundle (Warning 14.2.11)
rubrics_metrics.description: A locally free subsheaf of a locally free sheaf does not always correspond to a subvector bundle; cokernel may fail to be locally free. Example: exact sequence 0 → t k[t] → k[t] → k → 0 on A^1_k.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish between 'injection of locally free sheaves' and 'injection of vector bundles' — the latter requires cokernel to be locally free.

rubrics_metrics.name: Triviality of vector bundles on A^1 (Exercise 14.2.N)
rubrics_metrics.description: Every finite rank n vector bundle on A^1_k is trivial of rank n (use classification of finitely generated modules over PID).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise warns to ensure finite generation before applying the PID structure theorem; motivates generalizations to higher affine spaces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subscheme cut out by a section (Exercise 14.2.O)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a section s of a locally free sheaf F on a scheme X, one can define the subscheme V(s) cut out by s = 0; the definition should be independent of choices/trivializations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two approaches: coordinate description using local trivializations or intrinsic description as the largest closed subscheme where s restricts to 0.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hartogs-type extension for locally free sheaves (Exercise 14.2.P)
rubrics_metrics.description: On a locally Noetherian normal scheme, sections of a locally free sheaf defined away from a closed set of codimension at least 2 extend over that set (algebraic Hartogs lemma).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relies on Theorem 12.3.14 and normality hypotheses; used to control sections in codimension ≥2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regularity of rational sections of invertible sheaves (Exercise 14.2.Q)
rubrics_metrics.description: If s is a nonzero rational section of an invertible sheaf on a locally Noetherian normal scheme and s has no poles, then s is regular.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hint: use Exercise 13.5.H; standard fact about divisors and invertible sheaves on normal schemes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Behavior of locally free sheaves in short exact sequences (Exercises 14.2.R–S)
rubrics_metrics.description: If 0 → F' → F → F'' → 0 is an exact sequence of quasicoherent sheaves and F', F'' are locally free, then F is locally free. Conversely, if F and F'' are locally free, F' need not be locally free (counterexample given).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Locally reduce to affine Spec A with free modules and use matrix rank/determinant arguments; transition matrices for F become block upper triangular with blocks for F' and F''.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tensor algebra, symmetric and exterior algebras preserve local freeness (Exercise 14.2.T,14.2.U,V)
rubrics_metrics.description: If F is locally free of rank m, then T^n F, Sym^n F and ∧^n F are locally free and their ranks follow the usual formulas; determinant det F := ∧^{rank F} F is a line bundle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercises construct filtrations for Sym^r and ∧^r of short exact sequences with specified subquotients, and show determinant behaves well in exact sequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perfect pairing between wedge powers (Exercise 14.2.W)
rubrics_metrics.description: For F locally free of rank n there is a map ∧^r F × ∧^{n−r} F → ∧^n F inducing an isomorphism ∧^r F ≅ (∧^{n−r} F)^∨ ⊗ ∧^n F (perfect pairing of vector bundles).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Generalizes perfect pairings of finite-dimensional vector spaces; used in duality arguments (e.g., Hodge duality type statements).

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternating product of determinants trivial in finite exact sequences (Exercise 14.2.X)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a finite exact sequence of finite rank locally free sheaves, the alternating tensor product of their determinant line bundles is trivial: ⊗_{i} det(F_i)^{(−1)^{i}} ≅ O_X.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proved by breaking sequence into short exact sequences and applying the filtration results for wedge powers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extend tensor algebra constructions to quasicoherent sheaves (Exercise 14.2.Y)
rubrics_metrics.description: Define T^n F, Sym^n F, and ∧^n F for a quasicoherent sheaf F (e.g., by describing them on affines and checking localization compatibility).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives a way to work with these standard algebraic constructions beyond locally free sheaves.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hom preserves quasicoherence/coherence under finiteness hypotheses (Exercise 14.3.A)
rubrics_metrics.description: If F is finitely presented (quasicoherent) and G quasicoherent then Hom(F, G) is quasicoherent; if G is coherent and O_X coherent then Hom(F, G) is coherent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use local finite presentations of F and left-exactness of Hom; counterexamples exist when hypotheses fail (text gives a valuation ring example).

rubrics_metrics.name: Duals of coherent sheaves (14.3.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: If F is coherent then its dual F^∨ := Hom(F, O_X) is coherent; there is a canonical double dual morphism F → F^{∨∨}, and sheaves for which this is an iso are called reflexive (not used further).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Double dual need not be an isomorphism in general (example: coherent sheaf from k[t]/(t) on A^1 has zero dual).

rubrics_metrics.name: Isomorphism Hom(F, G) ≅ G ⊗ F^∨ for finite rank locally free F (Exercise 14.3.B)
rubrics_metrics.description: If F is finite rank locally free and G is quasicoherent, then Hom(F, G) ≅ G ⊗ F^∨.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard identification used to simplify Hom computations when source is locally free of finite rank.

rubrics_metrics.name: Left-exactness of Hom in exact sequences when target is locally free (Exercise 14.3.C)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given 0 → F → G → H → 0 exact with H locally free, then 0 → Hom(H, E) → Hom(G, E) → Hom(F, E) → 0 is exact (except possibly on the right a priori, but is exact in this setup).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof reduces to affine case where sequence splits; yields exact sequences of duals for coherent sheaves when hypotheses hold.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support of finite type quasicoherent sheaf is closed (Exercise 14.3.D)
rubrics_metrics.description: The support of a finite type quasicoherent sheaf on a scheme X is a closed subset; in contrast, the support of an arbitrary quasicoherent sheaf need not be closed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise gives examples and cautions; relies on finite generation to get closedness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geometric Nakayama (Exercise 14.3.E)
rubrics_metrics.description: If F is a finite type quasicoherent sheaf and a_1, ..., a_n ∈ F(U) have images that generate the fiber F|_p at p, then there exists an affine neighborhood Spec A of p where these sections generate F in the following senses: (i) generate F(Spec A) as an A-module; (ii) generate each stalk F_q and each fiber F|_q over Spec A.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consequences: if the fiber at p is 0 then there is a neighborhood where F is zero. This is the geometric formulation of Nakayama's lemma.
